note: Irregularities found while checking the 2026-11-17 brief against the tree. None of them blocks a merge; all of them are published on board/flagged.html with the source that establishes each one. The distinction this file keeps: a FLAG is something observed, a QUESTION (board/questions.json) is something unknown, and a SUGGESTION (board/suggestions.json) is something not yet chosen. Nothing moves between the three without evidence.

rows.title: Two of the five supplied products exist in no file in this repository
rows.what: link.amazon/B0c8moW59 and link.amazon/B0f3GKalj appear in no .json, .html, .md or .py file in the tree before this session. The register the rest of the site is generated from holds three products; the brief names five.

rows.why_it_matters: Two surfaces now describe the same project with two different product counts, and there is no rule reconciling them. This repository has already shipped two defects of exactly this class — a page printing a page count that had drifted from the tree it described.
rows.status: open — logged as CR-2 on the shared board, not actioned here

rows.title: An Associates tag is live on a minority of pages, and none of the five supplied links carries one
rows.what: {{tagged}} of {{pages}} published pages now carry a real Associates tag (shopnow047c-20), applied by session 7264f3c2 on 2026-11-17 — the first time any page in this repository has carried one. The remaining {{pages}} minus {{tagged}} carry only YOURASSOCIATEID or YOURID, the placeholders Amazon prints in its own documentation. Critically, **all five supplied link.amazon links still resolve without a tag**: the tag reaches the pages this site wrote, not the short links the owner supplied.
rows.evidence: Measured across every published page; all five supplied links fetched live 2026-11-17.
rows.why_it_matters: Amazon states the tags must be embedded in the product links on the declared site, and reviews an application only after three qualifying sales in 180 days. No tag means no attributed sale, which means no review. The brief now supplies a tracking ID for the first time, which is the missing value — but see BQ2-01: supplying a string is not the same as confirming it is an issued, active ID.
rows.status: partly resolved 2026-11-17 by session 7264f3c2 — the tag exists and is live; it does not yet reach the supplied links
rows.owner_action: Confirm in Associates Central that shopnow047c-20 is active for the intended marketplace (BQ2-01 is still open), then decide BS-01 to carry it across the remaining pages — and establish whether a link.amazon short code can carry a tag at all, which no source in this repository confirms.

rows.title: The rule that is supposed to stop a page printing a product price never fires
rows.what: Four copies of the context-aware price rule strip HTML tags before splitting the page into units on those same tags. After the strip there is nothing left to split on, so every page collapses to a single unit — and because almost every page mentions commission, earn or rate somewhere, the program-economics exemption then swallows any product price on it. Measured across the tree: {{price_rule_collapsed}} of {{pages}} pages collapse to one unit, so the rule cannot fire on any of them.
rows.evidence:
The inverted order is at .github/workflows/pages.yml:155, tools/validate_data.py:550, tools/build_readiness.py:623 and tools/validate_audit.py:272 - each reads re.split(r"|

||", re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", text)). Reversing the two operations makes the rule fire: a paragraph that offers the product at a dollar figure inside a buying context is flagged under the corrected order and passes silently under the current one. This board's own gate was written the corrected way round, and its negative test caught this very paragraph on its first run - the corrected rule works, and that is how the defect in the other four copies was noticed.
rows.why_it_matters: The site's no-prices rule is one of the four things every session asserts about every deploy. It is currently asserted by a check that cannot fail. No page is known to print a price today — this is a hole in the fence, not a breach — but the hole is in all four copies, including the one that gates every push to main.
rows.status: open — logged as CR-4 on the shared board, not actioned here
rows.owner_action:
In each of the four places: build the units by splitting the raw text first and stripping tags from each unit afterwards, i.e. [re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", u) for u in re.split(r"|

||", text)]. tools/validate_board.py already does it that way and its negative test proves the check fires.

rows.title: Two namespaces count 'tagged pages' with different rules and report different numbers
rows.what: tools/validate_brief.py matches the tag on the bare pattern tag=[A-Za-z0-9]+-[0-9]{2}, which fires on the shape wherever it appears — including inside a sentence about tags. tools/build_board.py and tools/validate_data.py match [?&]tag=, which fires only on a real URL parameter. The two therefore disagree about the same tree, and the gap is not a rounding difference: it is whether a page that merely discusses a tag counts as carrying one.
rows.evidence: Observed while recording BQ2-01 on 2026-11-17. A sentence that quoted the tag as it appears in a URL was counted as a tagged page by the design-brief gate and not by this board's measurement, which reported one fewer. Two other pages in the repository — pages/flags.html and release/index.html — quote the same string in prose and are counted the same way. The sentences have been left as they are, since they are not this session's to edit; the rule is what is wrong.
rows.why_it_matters: The tagged-page count is the one number that decides whether the revenue side of this site works at all. A reader who compares the design brief's summary with the decision board's register will find two different figures and no way to tell which is right — which is how a number stops being evidence and becomes decoration.
rows.owner_action: Agree one rule — a tag counts only when it is a parameter of an outbound Amazon link — and apply it in both places. The sentence in BQ2-01 is the test case: it must not count.
